$comment: Executable risk config. `metrics` name what gets measured (continuous values, not booleans); `rules` map a metric onto a 0-1 contribution via a scale; `profiles` weight the rules per buyer type. The scoring engine reads this file, so recalibration is a data change. `signal_inventory` below is the reference catalogue the rules are being migrated from.
status: draft - weights are opinion, not calibration

problem_statement.observed: 19 of 20 sampled subnets grade F; the exception scored 76 against an F threshold of 80.
problem_statement.cause: Scoring is additive and uncapped, and the heaviest findings are the most common ones. TAKEOVER_WINDOW_OPEN (CRITICAL, 40pts) fires on 90% of subnets because it is purely a function of subnet age. A typical subnet collects 85 points from four near-universal findings before anything actually wrong is found; F begins at 80.
problem_statement.consequence: The grade answers 'is this a mature Bittensor subnet' rather than 'is this a risky purchase'. Rare, actionable findings (RIVAL_CAN_SEIZE_NOW, OWNER_PROXY_RIGHTS, EXIT_PRESSURE - all 5%) carry the same or less weight than universal background conditions.
problem_statement.not_caused_by_the_indexer: Our SN38 run reproduces the README's own documented grades (D without provenance, F with), so this is upstream grading behaviour, not an artifact of the ClickHouse data layer.

base_rate_sample.method: indexed path, no provenance (provenance only adds findings, so grades would be equal or worse)
base_rate_sample.caveat: 20 of ~130 subnets. Indicative, not calibrated - a full-network pass is the prerequisite for real weighting.

personas.purchaser: Buying the subnet slot. Cares about losing ownership, levers the seller keeps after the sale, and whether the slot is defensible once bought.
personas.investor: Buying alpha, not the slot. Cares about dilution, dump risk, owner cash-out behaviour, and whether they can exit at their own size.

proposed_axes.label: Can control change hands - how fast, at what cost, by whom
proposed_axes.rationale: A subnet can be economically healthy and still be takeable on Tuesday.

proposed_axes.label: Is this being drained or dying
proposed_axes.rationale: A subnet can be unseizable while the owner exits into your bid.

axis_rationale: Collapsing both axes into one letter is a large part of why every subnet grades F. They are independent failure modes and a buyer needs them separately.
next_steps: Batch 2 candidate Q (drain-then-swap) - separates compromise from exit.
Build scoring.py: read this config, emit per-axis per-profile scores.
Run the full network to replace opinion weights with measured rarity, then recalibrate the bands.
Migrate the remaining signal_inventory entries into metrics + rules.
Before signal F: either verify wallet_pnl_event_log on the target host, or replay cost basis from alpha_trades.
host_caveat: Measured against the host in .env, which is PROD (per the operator). Base rates are therefore prod-measured; the remaining caveat is sample size (20 of ~130 subnets), not environment.

current.plain_english: The subnet is old enough that the ownership-transfer mechanism is switched on. Nothing more.
current.rationale: An age fact wearing a CRITICAL badge. Half the F threshold, on 90% of subnets. It means the mechanism is armed, not that anyone is attacking.

current.plain_english: Same as above, but the subnet's first birthday has not arrived yet.
current.rationale: A diary note, not a risk.

current.plain_english: Someone already holds enough to take the slot without buying anything more.
current.rationale: This is the headline risk the tool exists to find, and it is rare enough to be informative.

current.plain_english: A non-owner has actually locked conviction toward taking the subnet.
current.rationale: Locked intent is strictly stronger evidence than held capacity.

current.plain_english: The owner's locked defence is small next to the takeover bar.
current.rationale: Only meaningful paired with an actual challenger. Weak defence against nobody is not a risk.

current.plain_english: A single outsider holds more alpha than the owner does.
Several wallets are provably one entity, on funding, timing or proxy evidence.
current.rationale: This is precisely what defeats a naive cap-table read, which is the tool's reason to exist.

current.plain_english: Wallets that look coordinated but chain state cannot prove it.
current.rationale: An honest statement of uncertainty. Valuable to report, wrong to score as if confirmed.

current.plain_english: The top few holders could clear the takeover bar if they acted together.
current.rationale: Near-universal, and it assumes strangers cooperate. Low information.

current.plain_english: Ownership is concentrated (HHI over the cap table).
Alpha parked on hotkeys holding no UID - invisible to dashboards and to the metagraph.
current.rationale: Genuinely hidden inventory; exactly where quiet accumulation would sit.

current.plain_english: If the largest holder sold, the price would fall a long way.
Thin liquidity relative to the positions held.
A small number of hotkeys receive most of the emission.
current.rationale: This is what a normal validator set looks like.

current.plain_english: One entity holds a majority of validator weight, so it controls consensus.
current.rationale: Control of consensus is control of the subnet in every practical sense short of the ownership record.

current.plain_english: Childkey changes are queued and will apply automatically after their cooldown.
current.rationale: Near-universal as a bare fact. The risk is specifically a pending change whose target is OFF this subnet - score that, not the presence of a queue.

current.plain_english: Stake weight is being routed to hotkeys outside the subnet.
The slot is leased to someone else.
current.rationale: Never fired on mainnet - SubnetLeaseCreated has no occurrences in all history. Correctly severe if it ever does.

current.plain_english: Someone other than the owner can act as the owner.
current.rationale: Rare and severe - the seller keeps the keys after the sale.

current.plain_english: The owner coldkey is part-way through a swap to a different key.
current.rationale: The thing being sold may not be the seller's to sell by the time it settles.

current.plain_english: Root has switched off this subnet's emission; it earns nothing regardless of performance.
The subnet has never been started, or has been stopped.
New miners and validators cannot register until the owner reopens it.
The owner's share of emission accrues as liquid alpha instead of building takeover defence.
current.rationale: The cheapest defensive fix available to an owner, so its absence is informative about their posture.

current.plain_english: Squatted UIDs cannot be evicted for a long time after registration.
Validators are not setting weights.
Dead or idle UIDs are occupying slots that working miners could use.
Outcomes are driven by root stake rather than by participants in this subnet.
There is no room to bring your own validators in.
A ceiling on the largest holder the scan could have missed.
current.rationale: Always zero on the indexed path - attribution is complete, so the bound is not a hedge any more.

proposed.name: seizure_headroom
proposed.plain_english: The largest entity's LIQUID alpha measured against the conviction threshold - what they could lock today if they chose to.
proposed.catches: The buyer's blind spot: linked wallets holding more than enough alpha to lock and seize, who simply have not locked yet. Today conviction (locked) and alpha (held) are reported separately, so 'holds 3x the threshold, has locked nothing' reads as SAFE when it is the opposite.
proposed.notes: Must be computed per clustered ENTITY, not per coldkey, or wallet-splitting defeats it.

proposed.name: time_to_seize
proposed.plain_english: How long a challenger's freshly locked alpha takes to mature into enough conviction to win.
proposed.catches: Turns 'could seize' into 'could seize in N days' - the number that decides whether a defence is even possible.
proposed.notes: maturity_rate read 311,622 blocks (~43 days) on 2026-08-27. Verify the initial-conviction behaviour of do_lock_stake before quoting: it is unclear whether a fresh lock starts at zero conviction and matures, or starts at locked_mass.

proposed.name: owner_net_alpha_flow
proposed.plain_english: Whether the owner has been net selling their own alpha over 7 / 30 / 90 days.
proposed.catches: The retail blind spot: an owner quietly distributing into the market. Nothing in the tool today looks at owner behaviour over time.

proposed.name: owner_tao_withdrawals
proposed.plain_english: TAO moving from the owner to exchange-scale wallets.
proposed.catches: Cash-out behaviour that typically precedes abandonment.
proposed.notes: Exchange identification via funder fan-out (uniqExact(to_address)) - the same damping the clusterer already uses.

proposed.name: post_sale_headroom
proposed.plain_english: Recompute A on the assumption that you have bought the owner's position - is the slot defensible once it is yours?
proposed.catches: The actual question a purchaser is asking, which the current report never answers.

proposed.name: underwater_share
proposed.plain_english: What share of alpha is held below its cost basis.
proposed.catches: Dump risk. Underwater holders capitulate; holders in profit tend to sit.
proposed.notes: Cost basis must be REPLAYED from alpha_trades. wallet_pnl_event_log may be a shortcut but is an unverified MV - see source_policy.needs_verification. The P&L sidecars are absent on this host and unverified besides.

proposed.name: hot_money_share
proposed.plain_english: Share of alpha held by wallets created in the last 30 days.
proposed.catches: A durable holder base versus a rotating one.

proposed.name: concentration_trend
proposed.plain_english: Is ownership concentrating or dispersing over time?
proposed.catches: A subnet becoming more concentrated is becoming more seizable. A single snapshot cannot see direction.

proposed.name: rival_accumulation_curve
proposed.plain_english: The largest rival's position over time, not just today.
proposed.catches: 'Holds 14%' and 'went 2% to 14% in three weeks' are very different disclosures to a buyer.

proposed.name: proxy_grant_recency
proposed.plain_english: When the owner's proxy rights were granted.
proposed.catches: A proxy granted a week before the sale is a different animal from one held for a year. Currently reported as a boolean.
proposed.notes: Already available - the event replay carries granted_at_block.

proposed.name: owner_other_subnets
proposed.plain_english: Does this owner own or operate other subnets?

proposed.name: emission_share_trend
proposed.plain_english: Is the subnet's share of network emission rising or falling?
proposed.catches: The best single proxy for whether the thing is worth buying at all.

proposed.name: operator_churn
proposed.plain_english: Rate of miners and validators joining versus leaving.
proposed.catches: Operators leaving is the earliest decay signal, well before emission moves.

proposed.name: recent_childkey_changes
proposed.plain_english: Childkey changes made or queued in the last 30 days.
proposed.catches: Booby traps set shortly before a sale.

proposed.name: owner_rival_funding_distance
proposed.plain_english: How many funding hops separate the owner from the largest 'rival' holders.
proposed.catches: Whether the apparent rivals are actually the owner faking decentralisation - or genuinely hostile third parties. Both answers matter, in opposite directions.
proposed.notes: The current tool does exactly one hop and stops, an RPC-budget artifact. On the indexer the hop limit is arbitrary.

proposed.name: exit_feasibility_at_size
proposed.plain_english: Could YOU exit your intended position, at what slippage - not just 'would the top holder crash it'.
proposed.catches: EXIT_PRESSURE today models the largest holder's exit, which is not the question a retail buyer is asking.

proposed.name: drain_then_swap_pattern
proposed.plain_english: A large owner outflow followed within days by an executed coldkey swap.
proposed.catches: Distinguishes a COMPROMISE from a voluntary exit, which are otherwise identical on chain. The recovery signature is: single outsized sale at poor execution, then a coldkey swap. SN102: 145,105 alpha for 2,092 TAO in one transaction on 2026-07-12, swap executed 2026-07-21.
proposed.notes: Discriminate on the PATTERN, not the swap alone - swaps are common (3 of 3 owners sampled). Candidate tells: sale size vs the wallet's typical trade, realised slippage, and the gap between the sale and the swap.

seizability.label: Can control change hands - how fast, at what cost, by whom

value_decay.label: Is this being drained or dying

scoring.note: Each rule yields 0-1. An axis score is the weighted MEAN of its enabled rules, scaled to 0-100. A mean, not a sum: adding a signal changes the mix instead of inflating the total, which is the defect that makes 19 of 20 subnets grade F.
scoring.bands_note: Score bands are fitted to the observed population (p25/p50/p75 over the calibration run) so the middle of the scale reflects reality rather than judgment. But the TOP band is NOT a percentile: pure percentile banding forces a fixed share of subnets into F whatever the network actually looks like, which is the mirror image of the F-for-everyone bug. F is reached only by meeting a stated, absolute condition - so 'F' means a specific thing rather than 'worst 5% of whatever exists'.
scoring.direction_note: Scales encode direction by their own ordering: [[90,0.0],[1,1.0]] means fewer days is worse. There is deliberately no invert flag - one place to get it wrong instead of two.
scoring.unusable_rules_are_reported: A rule that cannot be evaluated appears under rules_unusable with a reason, and is excluded from the mean rather than scored as zero. Scoring a missing input as 'no risk' would make thin coverage look like a clean subnet.

bands_fitted_from.note: Refitted after the scale corrections. F is not a percentile - anchors only.

anchors.label: rival_lock_exceeds_bar
anchors.evidence: 2 of 129 subnets (SN24 1.36x, SN126 1.19x). Only 25 have any non-owner lock.
anchors.why: A non-owner has LOCKED more alpha than the takeover bar. Conviction asymptotes at the locked mass, so they cross the bar with certainty given time - the outcome is determined and only the date is open. rival_crosses_bar_in_days gives that date.
anchors.threshold_basis: Anchored on committed MASS, not on current conviction and not on liquid capacity. Current conviction understates a live takeover: SN24's rival has 700,000 locked against a 514,850 bar but only 215,835 conviction so far, a ratio of 0.42, because they are ~16 days into an ~84-day maturation. Liquid capacity overstates it: 20 of 129 subnets have a rival holding enough alpha who has locked nothing, and locking is public and slow enough to see coming. Decaying locks are excluded - with unlock_rate 0 their mass decays away and they accrue no conviction, which is why SN47's 112,345 does not count.

anchors.label: rival_lock_building
anchors.why: A non-owner has locked past half the bar. Someone is committing capital to this.

anchors.label: rival_has_the_means
anchors.evidence: 20 of 129 subnets - common, which is why it is D and not F.
anchors.why: A rival holds enough LIQUID alpha to clear the bar and you could not out-convict them after buying. Capacity, not intent: they have locked nothing, and locking is public and slow enough that you would see it coming. Price it, do not panic about it.

anchors.label: owner_liquidated
anchors.evidence: 13 of 128 subnets (10.2%); six of them hold exactly zero.
anchors.why: The owner sold at least 80% of everything they held over 180 days AND retains under 2% of the subnet. They have effectively left.
anchors.threshold_basis: BOTH legs are required because outflow alone confounds exiting with selling emission income: at outflow >= 0.7, 8 of 21 subnets still held 2.8-13.9% of eligible alpha and were plainly not exits. Median owner outflow is 0.041, so 0.8 is ~20x typical.

anchors.label: owner_partial_exit
anchors.why: The owner put more than half of what they held into the market over 180 days.

anchors.label: owner_key_drained
anchors.why: Nearly the whole owner position left the key shortly before a coldkey swap - the compromise-and-recover signature. Report the evidence, not a motive.

anchors.label: emission_switched_off
anchors.evidence: Of 38 emission-off subnets, most are mature - SN10 is 844 days old with 256 neurons and 3.4M alpha.
anchors.why: Pool-side emission has been switched off after the subnet had been emitting. Per the v450 storage doc this zeroes alpha_in, tao_in and excess_tao while LEAVING alpha_out, owner cut, root proportion and pending server/validator emission unchanged - so miners keep earning alpha while no new TAO backs the pool. Recoverable if root re-enables, which is why it is D rather than F for a slot buyer.

anchors.label: no_miner_earned
anchors.evidence: 38 of 128 (29.7%) are dead by this test.
anchors.why: No miner has earned in ~7 days. Validators are still paid on every such subnet, so an alpha holder is diluted to fund consensus over work that is not happening.

anchors.label: dead_subnet
anchors.why: Dead AND unbacked: no miner has earned in ~7 days and pool-side emission is off. Nothing is produced and no new TAO backs the alpha still being issued. Validators continue to be paid throughout, so the dilution does not stop.

anchors.label: emission_switched_off_investor
anchors.evidence: 35 of 128 (27.3%) - too common to carry an F.
anchors.why: Pool-side emission is off, so alpha is issued with no new TAO backing it.

anchors.label: no_miner_earned_purchaser
anchors.why: No miner has earned in ~7 days. Graded lower than for an investor on the same reasoning as emission being off: a slot buyer owns the thing and can recruit operators, whereas an alpha holder has no lever to restart it.

scoring.anchor_semantics: Anchors can only make a grade WORSE, never better. A subnet that scores well but meets an anchor is floored at the anchor grade, and the report must name which anchor fired and why. A subnet scoring badly is never rescued by failing to meet one.

anchors_not_used.rival_accumulating: Already scored as the RIVAL_IS_BUILDING rule; anchoring it too would double-count.

scoring.never_started_is_not_a_penalty: subnet_never_started (SubnetEmissionEnabled false AND FirstEmissionBlockNumber None) is deliberately NOT an anchor. A subnet awaiting activation is not damaged goods; conflating it with one that was switched off would grade ~3 new subnets as if they had been killed. Report it as context.
scoring.capacity_vs_intent: Three different quantities, easily confused, and each wrong on its own. LIQUID alpha above the bar is CAPACITY - common (20 of 129) and slow to act on, so it is D. Current CONVICTION is where a locker stands today and understates a fresh commitment (SN24 reads 0.42 on a takeover that is already determined). Locked MASS is the outcome, because conviction asymptotes at it - rare (2 of 129 above the bar) and irreversible enough to anchor F on. takeover_window_open is deliberately not an anchor at all: an open window is a possibility, not an event.

seizure_headroom_ratio.description: Largest non-owner entity's LIQUID (unlocked) alpha divided by the conviction threshold. 1.0 means they can seize today without buying anything.

time_to_seize_days.description: Days for a fresh lock to mature into enough conviction to win.
time_to_seize_days.resolved_from_source: do_lock_stake @ v450 writes a fresh lock with conviction 0, so it starts at zero and matures: conviction(t) = mass * (1 - exp(-t/MaturityRate)). Inverting gives blocks-to-threshold = -MaturityRate * ln(1 - threshold/mass); a mass at or below the threshold never reaches it, since conviction asymptotes at the locked mass. Also: with UnlockRate = 0 a DECAYING lock accrues no conviction at all and its mass decays to zero, so an attacker must call set_perpetual_lock(true).
time_to_seize_days.sparse: Returns null when the strongest entity cannot reach the threshold at all (conviction asymptotes at locked mass). Scoring must read null as NO RISK, not as a missing value.

owner_net_alpha_flow.description: Owner's signed net alpha flow over 7/30/90 days. Negative means the owner is net selling.
owner_net_alpha_flow.coldkey_lineage_required: MUST follow the owner's coldkey lineage backwards through executed swaps. A swap re-keys the position in one storage transaction and emits ZERO alpha_trades rows, so the post-swap key has no history behind it and a current-key-only read under-reports silently, to zero. This is the COMMON case, not an edge case: all 3 owners in the first sample had swapped (SN21 twice). Measured: SN102 scored 0.001 net selling on the current key while the previous key had been drained of 145,105 alpha.
owner_net_alpha_flow.window_rationale: 7/30/90/180d. Short windows miss slow or historical events - SN102's drain is invisible at 30d and obvious at 90d, because it happened 47 days before the run.

post_sale_defence_ratio.description: Alpha you acquire with the slot, against what you must out-convict to hold it. Below 1.0 means you are buying a subnet you cannot defend.

rival_accumulation.description: Share of the strongest rival's current position acquired inside the window. Turns a static holding into a trajectory.

drain_then_swap.description: Large owner outflow followed within days by an executed coldkey swap - the compromise-and-recover signature.

transfer_follow_through.description: Of alpha the owner moved out by transfer, how much the destinations then sold into the market. A transfer whose recipient liquidated is a disposal with an extra hop.

subnet_context.description: Flat facts the anchors test against. Not scored as rules.
subnet_context.requires_rpc: subnet_never_started / subnet_emission_switched_off need FirstEmissionBlockNumber, which has no indexer column. Without --rpc both are false and neither anchor fires -- fail-closed, so a missing read never invents a penalty.

miner_productivity.description: Whether the subnet rewards work, and to how many miners. Measured over ~7 days of snapshots, never at one block.
miner_productivity.window_note: Point-in-time is unusable: emission resets each tempo, so SN102 reads 0 miners earning at its latest block and 32% across seven days.

participation.description: Validator set size, diversity, agreement and earnings; miner operator concentration; and entity-level self-dealing between miners and validators.
participation.entity_level_note: Self-dealing is measured against CLUSTERS, not raw coldkeys. Coldkey overlap reads ~0% on every subnet sampled because anyone running both sides uses separate wallets; the clusterer is what sees through it.

RIVAL_CAN_SEIZE_NOW.plain_english: An entity holds enough liquid alpha to lock and take the subnet.

SEIZE_IS_FAST.plain_english: How little time an owner would have to react to a challenger.
SEIZE_IS_FAST.null_note: time_to_seize_days is null when the strongest entity can never reach the threshold - conviction asymptotes at locked mass. That is the safest state, not a missing reading.
SEIZE_IS_FAST.fitted_note: NOT mis-scaled despite the saturation flag. 106 of 128 subnets are null (the strongest entity can never reach the threshold - genuinely no risk); the 22 real values span 11 to 226 days, median 41, which the scale covers. The zeros are the population being mostly unseizable, not a scale defect.

OWNER_DISTRIBUTING.plain_english: The owner is NET selling their own alpha. Net, not gross: owners routinely cycle owner-cut emission through the market, which gross flow scores identically to liquidation.
OWNER_DISTRIBUTING.fitted_note: Refitted to the non-zero population (n=25 of 128): p25=0.008 med=0.105 p75=0.433 max=0.804. The prior scale topped out at 0.3, pinning the upper quartile of real sellers at 1.0.

CANNOT_DEFEND_AFTER_PURCHASE.plain_english: What you are buying cannot out-convict the strongest rival already present.

RIVAL_IS_BUILDING.plain_english: The strongest rival is actively accumulating, not sitting.

OWNER_KEY_COMPROMISED.plain_english: Most of the owner's position left the key shortly before a coldkey swap - the compromise-and-recover signature.
OWNER_KEY_COMPROMISED.reporting_note: Present the evidence, not a motive: a drain and an exit are the same shape on chain.
OWNER_KEY_COMPROMISED.discriminator_note: Sized by SHARE OF POSITION, not by execution quality. The SN102 theft used transfer_stake, which moves custody without touching the pool: realised price equals spot exactly, so an execution-vs-spot test reads 1.000 and discriminates nothing. Measured share of position separates the real case (0.984) from routine pre-swap activity (0.012).

OWNER_ALPHA_REACHED_MARKET.plain_english: Alpha from the owner's side reached the market, whether sold directly or moved to another key and sold from there.
OWNER_ALPHA_REACHED_MARKET.bounded_note: Share of everything held over the window that left for the market, so it cannot exceed 1. The earlier form divided by the CURRENT holding and returned 2.3+ on real subnets, pinning the scale and reducing the rule to a boolean.

NO_PRODUCTIVE_WORK.plain_english: Few or no miners are earning, so the subnet is not rewarding work.
NO_PRODUCTIVE_WORK.fitted_note: Population p25=0.000 p50=0.033 p75=0.265 p90=0.959 over 127 subnets. The prior scale was fitted to an 8-subnet sample containing SN102 at 0.32, which is p85 of the real distribution - it treated an outlier as the healthy baseline.

MINER_REWARDS_CAPTURED.plain_english: Miner emission is captured by a handful of UIDs rather than contested.
MINER_REWARDS_CAPTURED.gate_note: Gated on anyone earning at all -- concentration is meaningless when the numerator is zero.
MINER_REWARDS_CAPTURED.fitted_note: Gated to the 87 subnets with any earner; among those top-10 capture is overwhelmingly high, so the scale spans 0.5-1.0 rather than bottoming at 0.5.

FEW_VALIDATORS.plain_english: Consensus rests on a small number of independent validator entities.
FEW_VALIDATORS.fitted_note: Entity count p10=5 p25=7 p50=9 p75=12 p90=13 max=18.

VALIDATORS_NOT_EARNING.plain_english: Most validators are not receiving dividends.
VALIDATORS_NOT_EARNING.fitted_note: Earning share p10=0.625 p50=0.740 p90=0.862 - a tight band, so the scale must span it rather than 0-1.

MINERS_FEW_OPERATORS.plain_english: A handful of operators hold most miner slots -- a closed shop rather than an open market.

SELF_DEALING.plain_english: The same entities run the miners and the validators, so emission cycles back to the operator.
SELF_DEALING.fitted_note: 57 of 128 subnets have zero overlap. Among the 71 that do: p25=0.008 p50=0.020 p75=0.084 max=1.000. The prior scale started at 0.05 and so scored the entire real range as zero.

source_of_truth: subtensor pallet source at the spec mainnet is running (v450 at time of writing). Indexer scripts are a useful reference for query shape, but chain source decides semantics - both a vault note and a spec-440 checkout have already been observed to disagree with live behaviour.

source_policy.note: Tiered, not a blocklist. A source moves up a tier when someone verifies it, and the verification is the work - presence in system.tables is not evidence of correctness.

preferred.why: Base tables, exercised against chain state during this integration.

wallet_pnl_event_log.why: Materialized view. Possibly usable, but an MV can be redefined or rebuilt independently of the tables beneath it, so verify it is maintained on the target host and that its semantics match what the signal needs BEFORE depending on it. Where alpha_trades gives the same answer, prefer alpha_trades.

do_not_use_without_investigation.alpha_positions: not present on this host; correctness unverified
do_not_use_without_investigation.closed_legs: not present on this host; correctness unverified
do_not_use_without_investigation.wallet_daily_snapshots: not present on this host; correctness unverified
do_not_use_without_investigation.whale_snapshots: not present on this host; correctness unverified

chain_constants.note: Global chain values surfaced for context. They are identical across subnets, so they must never be scored -- a flat input adds noise to calibration and cannot discriminate.

interpretation_caveats.owner_selling_is_ambiguous: A drained owner key and an exiting owner are the SAME SHAPE on chain. SN102's -148,920 alpha over 90d was a COMPROMISE, not a cash-out: the key was hacked, dumped in a single sale, and swapped nine days later. Both are material to a buyer - the alpha hit the market either way - but they imply opposite things about the owner's commitment, so the report must present the evidence rather than assert a motive.

data_semantics.alpha_trades_direction_is_not_disposal: Three different events carry direction='sell' and must never be summed: a real market sale (is_transfer=0, moves the price); transfer_stake (is_transfer=1, custody moves to another coldkey, emits BOTH a sell and a buy leg, and tao_amount is a notional valuation rather than TAO received); and move_stake (same coldkey, an internal rebalance that is not a disposal at all). Measured on SN102: 148,819 of 148,920 alpha counted as 'sold' was transfer_stake and the actual market sale was 99.9 alpha - summing them invented a dump that never touched the pool. See also the indexer note data-model/alpha-trades-transfer-and-destructive-events.
data_semantics.a_transfer_can_be_a_sale_in_two_steps: Do not treat transfer_stake as a non-disposal. On SN102 the destination sold 100% of the 148,725 alpha it received (97,067 via remove_stake_limit, 51,974 via batch_all) and ended at a zero balance, realising ~1,293 TAO against a 2,142 TAO notional at transfer time - about 40% lost to slippage, which is precisely why a thief transfers before selling rather than selling from the victim's key. Follow the destination before classifying the transfer.

liveness_taxonomy.definition: 'Dead' means NO MINER HAS EARNED in ~7 days, on a subnet that has started. Emission being on or off is a SEPARATE axis (backing), not part of the definition - 9 subnets have emission off and miners still earning, and 12 have emission on and no miner earning. Conflating the two mislabels both.

working_unbacked.note: Producing, but alpha is issued with no new TAO behind it.

dead_funded.note: Resources still flowing, nothing produced for them.

dead_unbacked.note: Terminal: no backing coming in and nothing produced.

never_started.note: Embryonic, not damaged. Validator earning is 0.000 here too, unlike every dead bucket.

liveness_taxonomy.the_extractive_finding: On ALL 38 subnets where no miner earns, validators are still paid - median validator earning share 0.72 to 0.77, indistinguishable from the 0.75 seen on live subnets. So a dead subnet is not idle: it mints alpha and routes it to the validator set for securing a network that produces nothing. For an alpha holder that is the worst shape on the board - continuous dilution funding consensus over work. It is also why validator earning share cannot be used as a liveness test: it looks identical dead or alive.
liveness_taxonomy.why_not_validator_earning: validator_earning_share has p10=0.625 p50=0.740 p90=0.862 across the whole network and does not separate the buckets. Miner earning does.
